errors.reason: A 'Why' or comparative question title claims a cause or comparison without support in the indicator definition.

claims.text: How Does the USA Compare on Young Boys?
While in countries and territories like South Korea young boys make up 3.5 percent of the male population, in parts of Africa they approach 16 percent.
Central African Republic has 16 percent young boys. In Japan, it is 4 percent.
Central African Republic is the world's highest. Almost 1 in 6 males there is a child.
claims.support: Central African Republic rank 1 out of 208, value 15.977% (approx 1 in 6)

claims.text: It has 2.8 times the share of the USA, which has 5.8 percent.
claims.support: Central African Republic 15.977% / USA 5.797% = 2.756 (rounded to 2.8), USA: 5.8%

claims.text: This counts the male population between the ages 5 to 9 as a percentage of all males.
claims.support: Male population between the ages 5 to 9 as a percentage of the total male population.

claims.text: The lowest shares on Earth? Japan and Italy at 4 percent, and South Korea at 3.5 percent.
Somalia has 15.7 percent and DR Congo has 15.4 percent.
Do you see many young boys in your city?
